recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say which function is outside, which is inside, and why x > 0 is stated.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Differentiate the outer sine
steps.margin_note: First mark. sine is outside and log x is inside. The cosine keeps the same inside part, log x — it does not become cos x.
steps.memory_tip: Whatever is inside the sine stays inside the cosine, unchanged. Only the extra du/dx factor is new.
lines: f(x) = sin(log x),  x > 0, where log is the natural logarithm.
because log x is defined only for positive x.
Take u = log x. Then f(x) = sin u

recall.must_convey: That sine is the outer function, so f′(x) = cos(log x) times the derivative of log x.
accept: sin u differentiates to cos u times du by dx
the outside is sine and the inside is log x
cos log x stays with log x inside
sin bayata undi, log x lopala undi
differentiate the sine first and keep log x inside the cosine

steps.why: The mark is for identifying the layers correctly. Writing cos x instead of cos(log x) is a different function altogether, so this line is where the method is judged.
common_mistakes: Writing f′(x) = cos x instead of cos(log x).
Writing cos(log x) alone, with no inner derivative attached.

steps.label: Differentiate log x and finish
steps.margin_note: Second mark. d/dx(log x) = 1/x, so the cosine is divided by x. Since x > 0, dividing by x is always allowed here.
steps.memory_tip: log x inside produces a factor 1/x, so an x appears under the line in the final answer.

lines.text: (the standard derivative of log x, for x > 0)

recall.must_convey: That d/dx(log x) = 1/x, giving f′(x) = cos(log x)/x.
accept: log x differentiates to one by x
the answer is cos log x divided by x
an x comes into the denominator
log x ki one by x, kaabatti x kinda vasthundi
multiply by one over x at the end

steps.why: This mark is for the 1/x. Leaving it out gives cos(log x), which is the derivative with respect to log x, not with respect to x.
common_mistakes: Writing the answer as cos(log x)·log x by differentiating log x wrongly.

insider_note: One chain rule: cos of the inside, times the derivative of the inside. The condition x > 0 is stated because log x needs it, so keep it with the answer.
